Yes. The corpus supports prioritizing the Advanced OCR Pipeline before the Microsoft Teams integration.

- Scanned PDF processing is the primary driver of citation errors and customer onboarding delays, making the Advanced OCR Pipeline the "highest technical priority" for NovaLearn [NL-001#NL-001-S08].
- The OCR pipeline is described as a "critical system stability requirement," not a nice-to-have: 27% of support tickets in May were related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- Teams integration is still in an earlier stage: it is in the design phase for Q4 2026, with development slated for early 2027, whereas OCR is scheduled for release in August 2026 [NL-001#NL-001-S08][NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- Rushing Teams integration would risk delivering inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience and could endanger tenant-isolation security, because a secure Teams bot requires a complete redesign of the auth layer [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- NovaLearn's sales messaging already positions the Teams integration as a security advantage: unlike LearnPilot's connector, NovaLearn's Teams integration is designed to enforce active user permissions [NL-032#NL-032-S05][NL-032#NL-032-S02].

Business recommendation: Keep OCR first, keep Teams in Q4 design phase, and have Sales sell NovaLearn's citation accuracy and permission enforcement rather than an accelerated Teams launch [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
